paper.title: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
paper.central_claim: Intent-guided LLM search converts incomplete app UI Transition Graphs into a vector database of intent–trajectory knowledge that improves task success, decision accuracy and interaction efficiency as a plug-and-play module for mobile GUI agents, with training-free transfer to web and desktop and bounded offline extraction cost.
paper.claim_scope: System improvement with a secondary benchmark contribution; not merely a retrieval-accuracy component. Preserve claims about incomplete graphs, real-time efficiency, cross-platform transfer and reliable successful paths when evaluating their evidence.

evidence.quote: We introduce KG-RAG, a Knowledge Graph-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that transforms fragmented UTGs into structured vector databases for efficient real-time retrieval.
evidence.support_explanation: Original method, incomplete-graph and efficiency framing; all remain part of the evaluated claim.

evidence.quote: However, AutoDroid does not fully leverage the UTG during execution for rapid retrieval of knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's closest-neighbor residual. AutoDroid already has offline UTGs and online LLM planning, so simply having a graph is not the distinguishing contribution. Its original fulltext is not in the shared reference bundle.

evidence.quote: For simpler English-language apps sourced from DroidTask Wen et al. (2024) , we utilize a 1-hour automated exploration per app using xTester .
evidence.support_explanation: Same-app offline environmental access is supplied before testing. Chinese apps receive eight-hour exploration each. Exploration is a real adaptation cost, despite no parameter retraining.

evidence.quote: Next, a powerful instruction-tuned LLM decomposes each high-level intent into a structured sequence of intermediate milestones.
evidence.support_explanation: Screenshots from the extracted graph feed VLM intent generation; milestone decomposition precedes candidate trajectory scoring. Model-assisted synthesis not human GT navigation validation.

evidence.quote: The highest probability in this distribution (corresponding to reaching a certain milestone) is taken as the trajectory’s progress score.
evidence.support_explanation: A maximum probability over counts 0..m measures confidence in some count, not the number of completed milestones. Inference: a confident zero-completion prediction could receive a higher primary score than a less confident successful prediction. The restored softmax procedure does not fix this semantic mismatch.

Restored listing confirms a negative squared distance between probability-rank indices and descending milestone indices; it is a tie-breaker in prose, not an independent check that the path executes or completes the intent.

evidence.support_explanation: Restored search has queue expansion, duplicate/loop removal, threshold addition to valid_trajectories and top-K queue retention. Prose says below-threshold paths are pruned, but pseudocode does not explicitly restrict the next queue to accepted paths; depth is used and incremented without explicit initialization. evidence.quote: Each entry in our structured vector database is a key–value pair: the key is a high-dimensional embedding of an intent discovered offline, and the value is the corresponding trajectory (sequence of UI actions to fulfill that intent).
evidence.support_explanation: Persistent artifact and later read location explicit; user instruction encoded with same text embedder, cosine top-K paths placed in online context. Embedding paragraph also says intent along with trajectory encoded, leaving exact key composition ambiguous.

evidence.quote: Success Rate (SR), which measures the percentage of user instructions successfully completed
evidence.support_explanation: SR/DA/AS named and defined at a high level, but no executable completion checker, human-judging procedure, validation, reset policy or maximum online step cap specified anywhere in the complete supplied text. These omitted details cannot be reconstructed from outcome percentages.

Counterexample to universal per-app accuracy gain: File Manager DA falls 80→73.33. Aggregate GPT-4 SR66.94→75.80, DA76.53→84.55, AS4.49→4.10; 162 source tasks across12 apps. Table's Average equals the unweighted mean of twelve app rows, not a disclosed pooled task SR; e.g. SR8.86 points not 8.9% relative.

evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported mobile-built memory transfer without retraining: +40/+20 SR percentage points, not40%/20% relative. No task count, held-out query audit or completed-state judgment protocol. Limitations paradoxically still list web/PC adoption as future work, so the detailed transfer protocol needs clarification.

Single-app Weibo extraction ablation1/2/4/8h supports SR/DA saturation at4h in that setting, while steps still improve at8h. No measured embedding/LLM search cost, retrieval latency, storage, update amortization or uniform data-budget comparison.

evidence.quote: No Authentication Required: We evaluate only logged-out scenarios and never use accounts, passwords, or authenticated actions;
evidence.support_explanation: Meaningful explicit scope boundary; purchasing/account-state tasks not established. Privacy safeguards are author reports, not independently audited.

evidence.quote: Since the workflows are fully induced before test-time inference, the agent uses the same workflow memory
evidence.support_explanation: AWM already induces and reuses offline workflow memory in later test tasks; retained textual procedures are not unique to KG-RAG. Comparison limited to mechanism, not reproducing or rejudging AWM results.

evidence.quote: For APIs requiring no extra parameters except the by default Playwright page instance, we execute the API directly as a standalone unit test.
evidence.support_explanation: SkillWeaver provides an adjacent exploration→retained skill route with explicit practice/testing; KG-RAG instead scores/summarizes graph paths and retrieves them as context, without disclosed real path re-execution before acceptance. No claim of numerical head-to-head superiority is made from different benchmarks.

signatures.object: App-specific extracted UI graph and accepted navigation-memory candidates
signatures.information: Automated xTester exploration exposes UI metadata/widgets/actions, graph links and screen images before test;1h per English app and8h per complex Chinese app. VLM/LLM see graph/screenshot-derived candidate information, not a documented held-out query split.
signatures.operation: Generate plausible screen intents; decompose into milestones; batched bounded BFS over UTG paths removes loops/duplicates; LLM logits softmax over milestone counts; use maximum probability as progress and rank-distance proximity as tie-breaker; threshold valid paths and retain top-K queue candidates; summarize paths.
signatures.output: Intent–trajectory pairs in persistent per-app vector database
signatures.conditions: Graph coverage and correct transitions; calibrated milestone scoring; compatible task/current-state preconditions; usable embedding similarity.
signatures.feedback: LLM-predicted counts and similarity, not disclosed real execution verification of accepted candidate paths.
signatures.selection_rule: score≥threshold adds valid_trajectories; top-K by score preferring shorter paths updates BFS queue; exact threshold and parameters absent.
signatures.selection_data: Offline app exploration and synthetic screenshot intents; benchmark query exclusion and version split not reported.
signatures.persistence: Summaries/trajectories and intent embeddings stored in per-app repository; no policy-weight update.
signatures.later_use: Cosine top-K query-intent retrieval conditions existing GUI agent decisions.
signatures.claimed_effect: Reduce online exploration and recover actionable paths even from incomplete graphs.
signatures.failure_boundary: Maximum class probability need not track progress; queue-pruning ambiguity; no demonstrated repair of missing edges, no calibrated gate/current-state validator/staleness recovery.

signatures.information: Current user task plus retained graph-derived path guidance; base policy/perception kept within Table5 paired rows, though exact prompts not supplied.
signatures.operation: Encode user instruction in same embedding space; cosine nearest-neighbor retrieval; supply associated action path as contextual navigation guidance.
signatures.output: Actions in current app, reported SR/DA/AS
signatures.conditions: Retrieved intent matches task and platform/current state; old app transitions remain valid; base agent can ground retrieved advice.
signatures.feedback: Reported task/decision outcomes but unspecified final success evaluator and no per-step mismatch/fallback protocol.
signatures.selection_rule: Top-K cosine similarity; no threshold for refusing unhelpful retrieval disclosed.
signatures.selection_data: Per-app stored synthetic paths; embedding selection based on Table8 downstream benchmark results.
signatures.persistence: Static memory at online test time; no successful online outcome accepted into memory in the described algorithm.
signatures.later_use: Reused across tasks/backbones; mobile-built memory reportedly transfers to two non-mobile GUI settings.
signatures.claimed_effect: Better success/accuracy with fewer actions, training-free plug-and-play transfer.
signatures.failure_boundary: QQ Music UI-TARS SR unchanged, File Manager DA worse; no validated output checker, separated dev/test selection, latency or repeated-run evidence.

gap.author_gap: Generic mobile agents lack app-specific navigation knowledge; fragmented UTGs are insufficiently extracted/integrated for fast online guidance.
gap.checked_gap: Persistent workflow memory and autonomous exploration/retained skills pre-exist (AWM and SkillWeaver directly read); AutoDroid already has offline UTGs (as reported in P1). Residual specific to KG-RAG is converting app graph structure through intent/milestone-guided candidate search into an embedding-retrievable navigation bank; not invention of graph memory, retrieval or retention themselves.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Offline intent/path bank provides C03 reference substrate; common learned text embedding space selects relevant trajectories; retrieved path conditions a frozen base GUI policy for each task.

No policy-weight training, no proven category holdout and no online persistent update.
